subject: C15
required_fixes: R1 — Prisma mutation admission is bypassed with workbench/manual credentials. crates/desktop-core/src/workbench/admission.rs:438 returns operation=None whenever tenant secret references are absent; authority/workbench_domain/send.rs:547 then dispatches without review. Registered-origin classification is also unavailable when context is omitted or the management credential is not ready (send.rs:180). This contradicts DESIGN.md:1593 and C15's explicit manual-credential requirement: a literal Authorization header or collection-owned credential can send a known Prisma mutation, and unknown registered-origin operations are not denied. Classify registered destinations independently of credential ownership/readiness, and prevent generic redirect hops from bypassing that classification. Acceptance: literal/manual, collection-Keychain and anonymous requests to registered known mutations require exact native review; unknown operations are denied; omitting context cannot bypass this; a generic redirect cannot enter a registered operation without admission; ordinary unregistered HTTP remains supported.

R2 — Managed requests accept ambiguous authority inputs. crates/desktop-core/src/workbench/admission.rs:39 omits Host from AMBIGUOUS, parse_url at :310 accepts URL user-info, and execute.rs:319/:722 forwards the resulting URL and headers. The locked reqwest 0.13.5 extracts user-info into Basic authorization; hyper-util 0.1.21 preserves a supplied HTTP/1 Host. A request can therefore carry an operator-controlled virtual host or an additional implicit credential despite admission of a different URL authority. DESIGN.md:1604 explicitly requires rejecting both. Acceptance: managed Host overrides, including case variants, and request URLs containing user-info are refused before secret access or token acquisition; valid requests still transmit only the admitted authority and intended authentication.

R3 — Context retirement does not cover managed workbench sends. authority.rs:1138 retires context-bound runtime work but not workbench reviews/transfers; workbench_domain.rs:624 reserves an unscoped operation. In workbench_domain/send.rs:600, check_review compares the pending and planned contexts without checking the current active context. Apply awaits file hashing after planning, then consumes the review and dispatches; transfer at :878 also awaits secret access/storage/token acquisition without a context-bound dispatch check. A tenant switch during those windows can leave an old review usable or send tenant A's operation after tenant B is selected. Acceptance: deterministic holds after planning and during credential/token preparation, followed by tenant switch, credential replacement or reset, retire the old review and prevent any not-yet-dispatched customer request; switching back cannot revive it. Already transmitted mutations retain truthful outcomes and are never replayed.

R4 — Response header redaction misses actual wire credentials. crates/desktop-core/src/workbench/execute.rs:481 builds redactions from source secret values, but the minted OAuth bearer at :686 and encoded Basic authorization are never added. The response-header projection at :841 consequently retains an echoed bearer token or Basic credential in RunRecord.headers, which is returned to React and persisted in history. The canary test at tests/workbench_execution/main.rs:708 only echoes the original raw secret, so it does not detect this leak. Acceptance: literal fixture responses echoing a minted bearer and a collection-Keychain Basic authorization value are redacted in the immediate result, history, ShowRun and post-restart projections; no derived credential is persisted in history metadata. Preserve the intentional encrypted response-body/download behavior.
evidence_gaps: T23 coverage is incomplete for C15's new execution lifecycle. tests/workbench_execution/main.rs:543 checks an immediate connection refusal, and the restart test/native C15-N08 checks interruption without replay, but the supplied C15 tests/native driver contain no offline-to-reconnected execution scenario. Provide source-bound evidence that reconnect alone sends nothing, preserves an uncertain mutation outcome and invalidates obsolete review authority, while a fresh explicit Send succeeds after reconnection. Retained C14 local-document coverage does not establish the new HTTP/history lifecycle.

The registered responsiveness method targets the selected request's URL field (evidence/C15/workload-budget.md), but tools/perf/measure_c15.py:208 and tools/perf/probe.swift:137 measure only the heading and path static text. The retained 20 samples therefore establish header visibility rather than the registered editor-ready target. Measure the registered URL-field condition, or retain a versioned rationale and owner/independent acknowledgement for the method change under T20 governance; do not relabel the existing samples.
limitations: Read-only review: inspected production source, tests and retained evidence; did not rerun builds/tests, launch the app, call endpoints, access credentials or implement fixes.

Independently recomputed all four supplied fingerprints, verified 528 source-inventory entries and 273 referenced artifacts, and checked run input/output hashes and predecessor bindings. The retained logs report 340 frontend tests, 134 Rust library tests, 9 HTTP integration tests and 5 focused Send tests passing; all 30 recorded mutation probes killed their mutations. These results do not cover the defects above.

Recorded native acceptance covers C15-N01 through N09 on executable eca83e71904e33f3fe67f7ffb591eab82e76bbf0c27d95ecd9bac4923dac471a. Performance samples are within numeric limits: response p95 701.14 ms, upload 94.29 ms, save 629.53 ms, reported responsiveness 39.72 ms and maximum process-tree RSS 327 MiB; the responsiveness method limitation is recorded separately.

Native evidence uses synthetic loopback services and staged collection/save-sheet paths. Production file-sheet interaction, spoken VoiceOver output, installed signed packages and live product qualification are not established by this review. The catalogue preserves 193 specifications, including 81 mutation-method entries; this is not live qualification.
